newsitem.title: UK: Wassall to float General Cable, return cash.
newsitem.headline: Wassall to float General Cable, return cash.

text.p: British diversified manufacturer Wassall Plc said Monday it planned to float shares in most of its General Cable Corp. unit in the United States and to return about 150 million pounds ($241 million) to shareholders.

At the same time, the company reported a 27 percent rise in its 1996 pre-tax profit to 65.9 million pounds ($106 million), excluding the impact from the volatile copper price during parts of the year.

Commenting on the plan to float the General Cable stake by way of an initial public offering, Wassall Chief Executive Christopher Miller said, "Our net investment in General Cable is $170 million. The value of the company to us as a result of the flotation is of the order of $750 million.

"This represents an outstanding return on our investment of only three years ago," he added, explaining that when Wassall acquired General Cable it raised 97 million pounds ($156 million) from shareholders and would now be returning substantially more.

General Cable's estimated value is based on an indicative pricing range already filed with the Securities Exchange Commission, but the final offer price and exact number of shares would not be fixed until the end of the offer period -- likely to be during May -- it said.
